Elina Svitolina and Gael Monfils are ending their marriage 💔

Elina shared this message on IG:

“This is the most difficult thing I have ever had to share.
Everyone knows how much Ukraine means to me. What I have rarely spoken about is what the war has done to me inside.
Last year, I told you I needed to step away from the court because I wasn't in the right emotional space. Today, I want to open up a little more. What you didn't see were the sleepless nights, the doubts, and the feeling of slowly losing myself.
Gaël saw all of it. He never let go of my hand. We fought through this together for a long time, with everything we had.
But some battles happen deep inside you, and no amount of love from someone else can win them for you.
With time, I came to understand that I need to find my way back to myself and that I cannot do that within our marriage. It is the hardest truth I have ever had to face and the hardest thing I have ever had to tell the person I love. Gaël listened. He has respected what I need with a strength and grace I will never forget.
Gael has loved me through my greatest joys and my darkest moments, and I have loved him with all my heart. Together, we built a beautiful life, and we were given the most precious gift of all, our daughter, Skai.
Skai will always come first. Our marriage is ending, but our family is not. We will always be her parents, side by side, at every step of her life.
Please know that there is no one to blame here. There are only two people who loved each other deeply and a story that is changing shape.
We ask for your kindness and for the space we need to heal.
Thank you for your love 🤍”

🇮🇱🇮🇷 Think Netanyahu lost? The exit polls just handed him the one result that keeps him in power long enough to restart the war with Iran

The bloc that wants him gone has the most seats on paper, but a chunk of those are Arab parties that no right-leaning Jewish party will sit with after October 7, so the math is a tie, and Likud itself came out bigger than expected by eating the seats of Ben-Gvir, Smotrich and the religious parties.

Shaiel Ben-Ephraim, former IDF intelligence officer, says that leaves Bibi holding the levers that matter:

"You've taken one of the most dangerous men in the world.

You put them in a desperate situation, but you've given them a lot of levers to get out of that situation."

Shaiel says Netanyahu's pre-election plan was to run an exact replica of the preparations that preceded the last two attacks on Iran, so Tehran would fire first, until the chief of staff vetoed it.

If no coalition forms, a caretaker government means he can start that war, use the crisis to pull Bennett and Lieberman into a unity deal, and if that fails, push the next election from spring into summer while Arab voters conclude their record turnout changed nothing.

He has broken Gantz and Mofaz the same way, and Shaiel expects him to do it again.

🇮🇱 Who actually won Israel's election? Nobody, and that keeps Netanyahu in charge long enough to restart the war with Iran

Arab parties just posted their strongest showing ever, the Eisenkot bloc gets the first crack at a coalition, and if both sides fail Israel votes again in early 2027 with Bibi running the country the whole way.

Col. Douglas Macgregor says Iran holding fire when Israeli jets crossed its border this weekend shows a military disciplined enough to honor a deal, and that discipline is exactly why Israel won’t wait:

“Iran seems to have gotten stronger and become more capable.

What is the incentive to wait?”

Douglas says there’s little daylight between Netanyahu and his rivals on Iran, a Democratic Congress won’t stop the war either, and the next round could run as a short blitz, a pause, then another burst.

His real fear isn’t the conventional munitions but the possibility Washington reaches for a tactical nuclear weapon when the strategy runs out.
